podcast.body: This song was part of a Spotify playlist compiled by Queen Mary University in London, which cataloged 700 songs with the highest likelihood of causing chills and/or goosebumps. The research indicated that sadder, slower, less intense, and more instrumental compositions tended to be most successful in evoking this physical sensation. "I will always love you by Whitney Houston."

podcast.body: Whitney Houston's "Titanic take" on the Dolly Parton standard became one of the greatest vocal performances in pop history, spending 14 weeks at number one from November 1992 through February 1993. This "athletic feat" returned to the Hot 100 after her death. It decisively defeated Tag Team's "Whoomp! (There It Is)" and UB40's "Can't Help Falling in Love" for the 1993 year-end title. "She poured her soul into her work. And this song really was an athletic feat. One of the greatest vocal performances in pop history."

podcast.body: Whitney Houston's cover of Dolly Parton's song for "The Bodyguard" soundtrack dominated the Hot 100 chart. Its immense popularity was a major factor in the soundtrack's blockbuster sales, contributing to 20 million copies sold in the US and 45 million worldwide. "When Whitney Houston dominated the Hot 100 with her cover of Dolly Parton's I Will Always Love You recorded for the soundtrack to Whitney's 1992 film The Bodyguard."
